items.stem: Hotelling’s T² is primarily used to test a population:
items.explanation: It tests a multivariate population mean vector against a specified vector.

items.stem: The one-sample Hotelling statistic contains which sample-size factor?
items.explanation: The standard one-sample statistic is n times the covariance-adjusted quadratic form.

items.stem: The usual sample covariance matrix S uses divisor:
items.explanation: The unbiased sample covariance matrix divides the centred outer-product sum by n−1.

items.stem: For a one-sample test with p variables, the numerator degrees of freedom of the F transformation are:
items.explanation: The numerator degrees of freedom equal the dimension p of the mean vector.

items.stem: If n=9 and p=2, the denominator degrees of freedom are:
items.explanation: The denominator degrees of freedom are n−p, which is 9−2=7.

items.stem: A paired multivariate test is reduced to a one-sample test by analysing:
items.explanation: Paired differences form one sample of multivariate observations for a one-sample mean test.

items.stem: For n=10, p=2 and T²=8, the transformed F statistic is:

items.explanation: The inverse of a diagonal matrix is diagonal with reciprocal entries.

items.stem: Which condition is required for the standard one-sample T² calculation?
items.explanation: The inverse S⁻¹ exists only when the sample covariance matrix is nonsingular.

items.stem: For d=(1,2)′ and S=diag(1,4), d′S⁻¹d equals:
items.explanation: S inverse is diag(1,1/4); the quadratic form is 1+4/4=2.

items.stem: Under the one-sample null, the exact transformed statistic follows:
items.explanation: The exact finite-sample one-sample transformation has numerator p and denominator n−p degrees of freedom.

items.stem: Which statements about the one-sample Hotelling test are correct?
items.explanation: A, C and D are true; B is false because the statistic includes the factor n.
statements: The sample covariance uses divisor n−1.
The one-sample F degrees of freedom are (p,n−p).

A.why: This is the defining one-sample statistic.

B.why: The sample-size multiplier n is part of T².

C.why: The conventional unbiased sample covariance uses n−1.

D.why: The numerator and denominator degrees of freedom are p and n−p.

items.stem: For p=3, n=12 and T²=9, F equals:
items.explanation: The multiplier is 9/[3×11]=3/11, so F=27/11≈2.455; option B is the closest value.

items.stem: For paired multivariate data, the null hypothesis is usually expressed as:
items.explanation: The paired procedure tests whether the population mean of the difference vectors is zero.

items.stem: The inverse covariance matrix in T² accounts for:
items.explanation: S inverse adjusts the squared distance for the variables’ variances and covariance structure.

items.stem: For p=2, n=6 and T²=10, the one-sample F statistic is:
items.explanation: The multiplier is 4/[2×5]=0.4, so F=4.

items.stem: Which statements distinguish the one- and two-sample procedures correctly?
items.explanation: A, C and D are correct. B is false because the pooled two-sample test has its own scaling and degrees of freedom.
statements: The one-sample statistic uses S from one sample.
The pooled two-sample statistic uses the same one-sample scaling unchanged.
A paired test can be applied to difference vectors.
The pooled two-sample F transformation has df (p,N−p−1).

A.why: The one-sample covariance is estimated from the single sample.

B.why: The two-sample statistic uses pooled covariance and a different scale.

C.why: Pairwise differences form a one-sample multivariate dataset.

D.why: This is the standard pooled two-sample denominator and numerator df pair.

items.stem: If S is positive definite, then d′S⁻¹d for nonzero d is:
items.explanation: The inverse of a positive-definite matrix is positive definite, so its quadratic form is positive for nonzero d.

items.stem: Which checks are appropriate before reporting a computed one-sample T²?
items.explanation: Check symmetry, nonsingularity and the n multiplier; positive determinant alone is not a complete general test in higher dimensions.
statements: Confirm S is nonsingular before inversion.
Confirm that the factor n is included.

A.why: A sample covariance matrix is symmetric by construction.

B.why: S must be invertible for S inverse to exist.

C.why: Off-diagonal entries are part of the covariance adjustment.

D.why: The factor n is required in the one-sample definition.

items.stem: For a one-sample Hotelling test with n=7 and p=3, the denominator degrees of freedom are:
items.explanation: The denominator degrees of freedom are n−p=7−3=4, so the correct value is option D.
